Let \(P(x, y)\) be a point on the locus. The condition is \(PA = PB\), so \(PA^2 = PB^2\).
\((x - 1)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = (x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2\)
\(x^2 - 2x + 1 + y^2 - 6y + 9 = x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 - 2y + 1\)
Cancelling \(x^2\) and \(y^2\): \(-2x - 6y + 10 = -4x - 2y + 5\)
\(2x - 4y + 5 = 0\)
The equation of the locus is \(2x - 4y + 5 = 0\).

Let \(P(x, y)\) be a point on the locus. \(P\) is equidistant from \(A\) and \(B\), so \(PA^2 = PB^2\).
\((x + 5)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (x - 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2\)
\(x^2 + 10x + 25 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = x^2 - 8x + 16 + y^2 - 2y + 1\)
\(10x - 4y + 29 = -8x - 2y + 17\)
\(18x - 2y + 12 = 0\), and dividing by \(2\),
The equation of the locus is \(9x - y + 6 = 0\).

Let \(P(x, y)\) be a point on the locus. Given \(AP = 2BP\), so squaring, \(AP^2 = 4BP^2\).
\((x - 2)^2 + (y - 0)^2 = 4\left[(x - 0)^2 + (y - 3)^2\right]\)
\(x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 = 4\left[x^2 + y^2 - 6y + 9\right]\)
\(x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 4 = 4x^2 + 4y^2 - 24y + 36\)
\(0 = 3x^2 + 3y^2 + 4x - 24y + 32\)
The equation of the locus is \(3x^2 + 3y^2 + 4x - 24y + 32 = 0\).

Let \(P(x, y)\) be a point on the locus. Given \(PA^2 - PB^2 = 13\).
\(\left[(x - 2)^2 + (y - 4)^2\right] - \left[(x - 5)^2 + (y - 8)^2\right] = 13\)
\(\left(x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 - 8y + 16\right) - \left(x^2 - 10x + 25 + y^2 - 16y + 64\right) = 13\)
The \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) terms cancel, leaving \(6x + 8y - 69 = 13\)
\(6x + 8y - 82 = 0\), and dividing by \(2\),
The equation of the locus is \(3x + 4y - 41 = 0\).

Let \(P(x, y)\) be a point on the locus. Since \(\angle APB = 90^\circ\), the segments \(PA\) and \(PB\) are perpendicular, so the product of their slopes is \(-1\).
Slope of \(PA = \frac{y - 6}{x - 1}\) and slope of \(PB = \frac{y - 5}{x - 3}\).
\(\frac{y - 6}{x - 1} \times \frac{y - 5}{x - 3} = -1\)
\((y - 6)(y - 5) = -(x - 1)(x - 3)\)
\(y^2 - 11y + 30 = -x^2 + 4x - 3\)
The equation of the locus is \(x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 11y + 33 = 0\).

When the origin is shifted to \(O'(h, k)\) with the axes remaining parallel, the new co-ordinates \((X, Y)\) of a point \((x, y)\) are \(X = x - h\), \(Y = y - k\).
Here \((h, k) = (2, 3)\) and \((x, y) = (1, 3)\).
\(X = 1 - 2 = -1\) and \(Y = 3 - 3 = 0\)
The new co-ordinates of \(A\) are \((-1, 0)\).

With the origin shifted to \(O'(2, 3)\), the new co-ordinates are \(X = x - 2\), \(Y = y - 3\).
Here \((x, y) = (2, 5)\).
\(X = 2 - 2 = 0\) and \(Y = 5 - 3 = 2\)
The new co-ordinates of \(B\) are \((0, 2)\).

When the origin is shifted to \(O'(h, k)\), the old co-ordinates are recovered from the new ones by \(x = X + h\), \(y = Y + k\).
Here \((h, k) = (1, 3)\) and the new co-ordinates are \((X, Y) = (5, 4)\).
\(x = 5 + 1 = 6\) and \(y = 4 + 3 = 7\)
The old co-ordinates of \(C\) are \((6, 7)\).

With the origin shifted to \(O'(1, 3)\), the old co-ordinates are \(x = X + 1\), \(y = Y + 3\).
Here the new co-ordinates are \((X, Y) = (3, 3)\).
\(x = 3 + 1 = 4\) and \(y = 3 + 3 = 6\)
The old co-ordinates of \(D\) are \((4, 6)\).

Let the origin be shifted to \(O'(h, k)\). Then the new co-ordinates satisfy \(X = x - h\) and \(Y = y - k\).
The old co-ordinates are \((5, 14)\) and the new ones are \((8, 3)\).
\(8 = 5 - h\), so \(h = 5 - 8 = -3\)
\(3 = 14 - k\), so \(k = 14 - 3 = 11\)
The origin is shifted to the point \((-3, 11)\).

The origin is shifted to \(O'(2, 2)\), so the old co-ordinates in terms of the new ones are \(x = X + 2\), \(y = Y + 2\). Substitute these in the given equation.
\(3(X + 2) - (Y + 2) + 2 = 0\)
\(3X + 6 - Y - 2 + 2 = 0\)
The new equation of the locus is \(3X - Y + 6 = 0\).

Put \(x = X + 2\) and \(y = Y + 2\) in \(xy - 2x - 2y + 4 = 0\).
\((X + 2)(Y + 2) - 2(X + 2) - 2(Y + 2) + 4 = 0\)
\(XY + 2X + 2Y + 4 - 2X - 4 - 2Y - 4 + 4 = 0\)
All the terms except \(XY\) cancel.
The new equation of the locus is \(XY = 0\).

Put \(x = X + 2\) and \(y = Y + 2\) in \(y^2 - 4x - 4y + 12 = 0\).
\((Y + 2)^2 - 4(X + 2) - 4(Y + 2) + 12 = 0\)
\(Y^2 + 4Y + 4 - 4X - 8 - 4Y - 8 + 12 = 0\)
The \(Y\) terms cancel and the constants give \(4 - 8 - 8 + 12 = 0\).
The new equation of the locus is \(Y^2 - 4X = 0\).

The slope of the line through \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\) is \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\).
\(m = \frac{3 - (-1)}{4 - 2} = \frac{4}{2}\)
The slope is \(2\).

\(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{-1 - 3}{2 - 2} = \frac{-4}{0}\), which is not defined.
Both points have the same \(x\)-co-ordinate, so \(EF\) is parallel to the Y-axis and its inclination is \(90^\circ\).
The slope is not defined.

\(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{1 - 1}{-3 - 7} = \frac{0}{-10}\)
Both points have the same \(y\)-co-ordinate, so \(GH\) is parallel to the X-axis.
The slope is \(0\).

An X-intercept of \(2\) means the line passes through \((2, 0)\), and a Y-intercept of \(3\) means it passes through \((0, 3)\).
\(m = \frac{3 - 0}{0 - 2} = \frac{3}{-2}\)
The slope of line \(L\) is \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

If \(\theta\) is the inclination of a line, its slope is \(m = \tan\theta\).
\(m = \tan 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)
The slope is \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

The slope is \(m = \tan\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the inclination.
\(m = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\)
The slope is \(1\).

Intercepts \(3\) and \(3\) mean the line passes through \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\).
\(m = \frac{3 - 0}{0 - 3} = -1\)
If \(\theta\) is the inclination, \(\tan\theta = -1\) with \(0^\circ \le \theta < 180^\circ\), so \(\theta = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ\).
The inclination of the line is \(135^\circ\).

Instead of comparing side lengths, compare slopes: two sides are perpendicular exactly when the product of their slopes is \(-1\).
Slope of \(AB = \frac{5 - 4}{3 - 4} = \frac{1}{-1} = -1\)
Slope of \(AC = \frac{-1 - 4}{-1 - 4} = \frac{-5}{-5} = 1\)
Slope of \(BC = \frac{-1 - 5}{-1 - 3} = \frac{-6}{-4} = \frac{3}{2}\)
Now (slope of \(AB\)) \(\times\) (slope of \(AC\)) \(= -1 \times 1 = -1\), so \(AB \perp AC\).
Also the three slopes are all different, so \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) are not collinear and do form a triangle.
Hence \(\angle BAC = 90^\circ\) and \(\triangle ABC\) is a right angled triangle, right angled at \(A\).

The inclination is measured from the positive direction of the X-axis. The positive Y-axis is already at \(90^\circ\), and the line is a further \(45^\circ\) anticlockwise from it.
\(\theta = 90^\circ + 45^\circ = 135^\circ\)
\(m = \tan 135^\circ = \tan(180^\circ - 45^\circ) = -\tan 45^\circ = -1\)
The slope is \(-1\).

Three points are collinear when the slopes of any two of the segments joining them are equal, so slope of \(PQ =\) slope of \(QR\).
Slope of \(QR = \frac{5 - 1}{4 - 2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\)
Slope of \(PQ = \frac{1 - (-1)}{2 - k} = \frac{2}{2 - k}\)
\(\frac{2}{2 - k} = 2\), so \(2 = 2(2 - k)\), giving \(2 = 4 - 2k\) and \(2k = 2\).
The value is \(k = 1\).

Slope of line \(AB = \frac{-2 - (-1)}{4 - 3} = \frac{-1}{1} = -1\)
If \(\theta\) is the inclination of \(AB\), then \(\tan\theta = -1\), so \(\theta = 135^\circ\).
The X-axis and line \(AB\) make angles of \(135^\circ\) and \(180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ\) with each other.
The acute angle between the X-axis and line \(AB\) is \(45^\circ\).

The line passes through \(A(x_1, y_1)\) and \(B(h, k)\), and its slope is \(m\). Since a slope is given, the line is not vertical, so \(h \ne x_1\).
By the definition of slope, \(m = \frac{k - y_1}{h - x_1}\).
Multiplying both sides by \((h - x_1)\),
\(m(h - x_1) = k - y_1\)
Hence \(k - y_1 = m(h - x_1)\), as required.

\(A(h, 0)\), \(B(0, k)\) and \(C(a, b)\) lie on one line, so slope of \(AB =\) slope of \(AC\). For the slopes to exist take \(h \ne 0\), \(k \ne 0\) and \(a \ne h\).
Slope of \(AB = \frac{k - 0}{0 - h} = \frac{-k}{h}\) and slope of \(AC = \frac{b - 0}{a - h} = \frac{b}{a - h}\).
\(\frac{-k}{h} = \frac{b}{a - h}\)
Cross multiplying, \(-k(a - h) = bh\), that is \(kh - ka = bh\).
Dividing throughout by \(hk\), \(1 - \frac{a}{h} = \frac{b}{k}\).
Hence \(\frac{a}{h} + \frac{b}{k} = 1\), as required.
